extracted.intended_audience: aspiring stand-up comedians (beginners to experienced performers) seeking training or coaching
extracted.subtask_description: Instructional curriculum and principles for writing jokes, building routines, and performing stand-up comedy (Level 1 → Level 2, crowdwork, MC skills), taught in-person, over Zoom, or on-demand using Greg Dean's proprietary methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke writing systems that simplify the creative process
rubrics_metrics.description: Joke writing systems that simplify the creative process
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Greg Dean developed three proprietary joke writing systems and coined the term “Joke Structure.” Examples named on the page include the Joke Prospector System and the Two-List Technique. These systems are presented as making joke writing accessible, repeatable, and rooted in craft rather than guesswork; they are the foundation of classes and the bestselling book Step by Step to Stand-Up Comedy. (Implied scoring: ability to use these systems to generate joke premises and punchlines reliably.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedic storytelling that connects with audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedic storytelling that connects with audiences
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction emphasizes storytelling techniques that emotionally and comically connect with listeners; classes teach how to craft stories that resonate on stage. The page highlights that storytelling is a core principle covered in class and is 'battle-tested' in performance venues like The Comedy Store.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance techniques that elevate stage presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance techniques that elevate stage presence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training covers stagecraft and delivery methods intended to elevate presence and effectiveness on stage. The copy stresses these performance techniques are informed by decades of live performing experience and tested at iconic venues, indicating emphasis on timing, delivery, and stage persona.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine building that turns ideas into polished sets
rubrics_metrics.description: Routine building that turns ideas into polished sets
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classes focus on taking scattered ideas and shaping them into cohesive, polished sets. Testimonials cite students going 'from scattered ideas to a full set that actually works.' The curriculum explicitly includes 'routine building' as a principle and promises a structured process to build a set from scratch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive, honest feedback that helps students grow with confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive feedback that helps students grow with confidence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program promises honest, supportive feedback as a core ingredient for improvement; student reviews repeatedly praise clarity of feedback and how it 'helps me level up.' This implies an evaluative standard: feedback should be constructive, actionable, and confidence-building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and clarity of instruction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site repeatedly emphasizes the clarity and structured nature of the teaching ('The structure and clarity of Greg’s classes are unmatched,' 'first structured curriculum for stand-up comedy'). Evaluative expectation: lessons should be organized, sequential, and make the process of building material explicit and teachable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical, repeatable, craft-based methods (not guesswork)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical, repeatable, craft-based methods rather than guesswork
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The method claims to make joke writing 'accessible, repeatable, and rooted in craft rather than guesswork' and to 'teach you how to think like a comedian.' The rubric favors techniques that can be reliably applied across topics and gigs, not ad-hoc or purely intuitive approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crowdwork: finding the funny in your audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Crowdwork — find the funny in your audience
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a dedicated 'Find the Funny in Your Audience' / Crowdwork ongoing workshop. This sets an evaluative standard for improvisational interaction and the ability to harvest and convert audience material into jokes in real time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level progression: foundational to advanced curriculum
rubrics_metrics.description: Level 1 → Level 2 progression (How to Build a Stand-Up Routine → Writing & Performing a Show)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommended learning path is starting with Level 1 (How to Build a Stand-Up Comedy Routine) then moving to Level 2 (Writing & Performing a Show). The rubric implies that competency is measured across a curricular ladder: basic joke/routine construction first, then advanced writing, show-building and performance skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: MC skills and hosting technique
rubrics_metrics.description: How to be a stand-up comedy MC
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A specific course 'How to Be a Stand-Up Comedy MC' is offered, indicating evaluative criteria for hosting gigs: segues, crowd control, pacing, and opening/closing other acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptability to performance formats (live, Zoom, on-demand)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to perform effectively across live in-person, live Zoom, and on-demand formats
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classes are offered live in Los Angeles, live over Zoom, and On Demand; this implies criteria for performing and delivering material that works across platforms (e.g., adjusting energy, timing, and audience interaction for virtual vs. in-person settings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of showcases and video reviews for evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Student showcases and video reviews as performance assessment tools
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program offers student showcases (At the Improv and on Zoom) and paid video reviews, indicating that recorded performance, audience reaction in showcases, and instructor video critiques are used as measures of progress and quality.
